content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "(continued) ## Monthly close calendar
Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2.
## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.
Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-estimates-for-sales-quotes-2026.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Estimating Token Volumes for Sales Quotes", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-09", "text": "title: Estimating Token Volumes for Sales Quotes

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

Included usage is the amount bundled with a package **during a billing period**. Charges apply only when:
1) a customer is on a plan that allows overage, and
2) usage exceeds included amounts.

- Self-serve: monthly, aligned to subscription start date (unless otherwise stated).
- Contracted enterprise: per order form.

content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "3/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Definitions (use these terms consistently)
- **Meter / billable unit:** The unit recorded by billing telemetry and used to produce invoices. Example: **billed_tokens** for Hosted API.
- **Raw tokens vs billed tokens:** Raw tokens may include uncached or pre-dedupe counts. **Billed tokens** are the invoicing unit after billing rules (dedupe/idempotency, cache-hit attribution rules, etc.). Credits and discounts apply to **billed** usage only.
- **Discount:** A reduction in price per unit (e.g., $/1M tokens) or a percentage reduction on usage charges.
- **Credit:** A dollar value that offsets charges on invoices (a “coupon” balance). Credits have **no cash value** and are not refundable unless required by contract or law.
- **Service credit:** A credit issued for SLA/non-conformance or billing errors.
- **Promotional credit:** A credit granted for trial, marketing campaigns, partnerships, or sales incentives.
- **Contracted credit:** A credit explicitly included in an Order Form/MSA as part of commercial terms."}]}

{"query": "late usage reaching warehouse after BD1 prior-period usage original dates invoice next month definition 2027 close calendar", "results": [{"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "## Late usage
Usage that reaches the warehouse after BD1 is not added to an issued invoice. It is billed on the next month's invoice as a separate line marked "prior-period usage" with the original dates, so a customer comparing a month's export to its invoice may see those requests a month later.
## Price changes
A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so.
The 2027 price book takes effect for usage from 1 March 2027: February 2027 and earlier usage is rated on the 2026 price book, and March 2027 usage onward on the 2027 price book."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "(continued) ## Monthly close calendar

## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.

body: ## Symptom
The Console invoice list sorts by the date an invoice was issued, not the period it covers, so a re-issued invoice for an earlier month can appear at the top.
## Workaround
Use the period filter or read the period on each invoice. Amounts and lines are correct.
## Status
Fix planned for the Console release in May 2027.

body: ## Scope
Invoices still unpaid after their due date, once any automatic payment retries have finished. Payments that fail during a payment-processor incident are retried automatically and are not overdue; this page doesn't apply to them.
## Schedule
| Days past due | Step |
|---|---|
| 3 | Reminder email to the billing contact |
| 10 | Second reminder; account team copied |
| 21 | Final notice |
| 45 | Hosted API access suspended until paid |
## Changes from 2026
From 1 January 2027 the final notice is sent on day 21 instead of day 30.

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}]}

For **March 2027**, Rosehip Data was billed **$2,140.00** for **21,000,000 billed tokens**: $1,880.00 for Hosted API usage and $260.00 for batch jobs.

The invoice is currently **open**, so that’s the amount billed, not a confirmed payment. March usage is counted in your account’s **America/Los_Angeles** timezone.
